Method — RM-009. Seven measurements against the working tree at ea31d45 on branch amit, four of them run in headless Chromium against the library as the dev server serves it. The openings — each of the ten wall-cutting catalog items loaded into a live page onto a wall of a 400 × 400 room, and its halfSize read after the loader had finished with it, which is the only reading that includes the ×300 branch; the same method applied to four ordinary items for U-3. The oversized hole — Shape, Path and ShapeGeometry called with the exact numbers those items produced, and the resulting bounding box and triangle count read; that is the three.js primitive Edge.createShape uses, exercised directly rather than through the viewer. The joins — a plan constructed headlessly with two walls of different thickness, its half-edge interior points and its room polygon compared, and the room's stated area compared against the shoelace area of its own interior corners. The file — Item.getMetaData read, and the catalog counted by script (168 items in eight placement types, 142 from models/gltf/, ten of types 3 and 7). What was not run: no renderer. U-2 is asserted about the geometry Edge builds and not about what a frame looks like, because the failure is a mesh that is the wrong size and a picture would only show that it is; and no procedural door was written, so every figure about the generator is an estimate rather than a measurement. Two planning inaccuracies were found and are recorded rather than fixed, since this is a planning pass: RM-007's per-wall height for half walls (U-5), which E2 had already measured out from under it, and the ×300 hack (U-3), which belongs to J1.

Method — RM-010. Nine measurements against the working tree at 6dd9665 on branch amit, six of them run in headless Chromium against the library as the dev server serves it. The roof — a 400 × 400 room loaded into a live page and all 31 meshes in the scene traversed for name, visibility, triangle count and bounding box, which is how “there is no roof” became a reading rather than an inference; the two implementations in three/floor.js were then checked against their call sites. The base elevation — every flat room-sized plane in that same scene collected with its y coordinate; there are two values, 0 and 250. The floor opening — a real room's interiorCorners pushed through Shape, Path and ShapeGeometry with F3's own stairwellHint() as the hole, triangle counts and bounding boxes read before and after, and the winding reversed to see whether it matters; then the same call with a hole straddling the outline, which is RM-009 U-2's test applied to a floor. The two models — a second Model constructed in a page that already had one, loaded with a different design, and both floorplans read back. The file — a design exported, re-loaded and re-exported, and the two strings compared. The filters — model/floorplan.js parsed into methods by script and each body matched against its seven collections. The coverage — coverage-summary.json from npm run test:coverage, per file. What was not run: no roof was generated and no level was built, so every figure about G1's and G2's own output is an estimate; and no renderer comparison — V-1 is asserted about what is in the scene graph, not about what a frame looks like. Two inaccuracies were found in the tree and are recorded rather than fixed, since this is a planning pass: the comment in three/floor.js claiming the roof is commented out when the line below it runs, and buildRoofUniformHeight(), a complete implementation nothing calls. Both are G2's to clear.

Method — RM-012. Nine measurements against the working tree at 38be485 on branch amit, all of them produced by running something and none of them read off a plan. The catalog — all 168 rows parsed and their keys counted, then every row's full cost taken the way check-budget.mjs takes it (the model, the thumbnail, and every distinct image the .glb's own JSON chunk names) and summed with each file counted once, which is what separates the 4,385,565 B the catalog occupies from the 4,746,822 B a naive per-item sum reports. The index — catalog.json compacted the way a bundler emits it and gzipped at level 9, then a synthetic augmentation built by adding a room, up to three tags, a {w, d, h}, a source, a licence and an author to each of the same 168 rows and gzipped by the same call, and the per-row figure multiplied out to 400 and 600. The containers — every .glb's JSON chunk read for extensionsUsed, which is how “152 already Draco” became a census rather than an assumption. The pipelines — npm run encode:check and npm run encode:textures:check run, and which put to the six command-line encoders. The predicates — all five called against a unit square and its centre, and every caller of each of them found across src/, then FloorItem.isValidPosition read statement by statement for its returns. The thumbnails — all 168 image headers decoded for their true dimensions rather than their filenames trusted, and the drawer's own panel width and grid read for what they are displayed at. The budgets — limits and measurements taken from tools/budget.json after npm run budget:update, and every projection computed against this catalog's own measured mean. What was not run: no acquisition, no pack, no import and no collision, so every figure about programme J's own output is a projection from this tree's numbers rather than an observation — the same caveat every planning pass in this set carries. Two of this document set's own records are corrected here: M-30, which RM-011 H1 already delivered as M-43 and which is withdrawn as a duplicate, and RM-007's framing of J4, which prices the polygon re-baseline as the risky half when the measurement puts the risk in the collision that does not exist yet. One repository inaccuracy is recorded rather than fixed, since this is a planning pass: Item.showError() has exactly one caller and that caller is unreachable, which makes it dead code with a comment claiming it fires. It is J4's to clear.

Method — RM-012, delivery. What J1 ran that the drawing above could not, since every figure about J1's own output was a projection until it existed. The provenance — each source established from evidence rather than resemblance and the evidence recorded in src/catalog/sources.json: the upstream furnishup/blueprint3d tree read over the GitHub API and all 25 js-glb basenames matched against it, Kenney's own page read for its file count and licence, every .glb's material names collected to find the shared 14-name palette that leaves exactly 140 when the two outliers are removed, and the Khronos sample set's README read for the duck. The unit — the whole catalog measured, then the small population's factor solved from six standard heights and cross-checked against a door frame measured independently in another kit; the earlier extent rule kept only as a 5 cm–6 m band. The keys — room and tags priced by adding each to the real 168 rows and gzipping at level 9 through the same call check-budget.mjs makes, which is how X-3's two estimates were found wrong. The thumbnails — all 168 rendered in headless Chromium over SwiftShader at 600 × 450 and box-filtered down, every output measured for coverage and edge contact rather than looked at, and both of the render's own free numbers — sphere fit against box fit, 3× against 2× — run over the whole catalog and decided on the bytes. The budgets — npm run build:demo then npm run budget:update, three times, once per commit. What was not run: no pack was acquired and no ceiling was raised for the thumbnails, so public-total and demo-total stand at 2.3 % and 1.8 % of headroom and J2 inherits that decision with the arithmetic beside it. Three of this document set's own records are corrected in place: X-3's prices for room and tags, and J1's own first slice, which read the Kenney kit as metres. One repository inaccuracy was fixed rather than recorded, since this is a delivery pass: Item.initObject's ×300, which RM-009 U-3 measured wrong and assigned here. And two are recorded rather than fixed. Two catalog rows ship on a licence nobody could establish, which is J2’s to decide. And useItemActions.duplicateSelected adds nothing: it reads meta.itemType and meta.modelUrl off Item.getMetaData(), which returns item_type and model_url — both reads are undefined, so Scene.addItem defaults the type to 1 and asks the loader for undefined. It went unseen because the test’s fake returns the camelCase shape the caller wishes for rather than the shape the real method returns, which is the second time in this document set a stub has agreed with the code instead of with the data. Found by reading who calls what while X-6’s survey was being checked; it belongs to J4, which owns copy, paste and duplicate, and it is not a typo — a duplicate also needs a new designId rather than the original’s, so the fix is a decision about what that re-add path reads.

Method — RM-012, J2 and J4 delivery. Ten tasks in nine commits, everything in J2 that does not require acquiring a pack and the whole of J4. The pack split — the catalog divided a second time and every row taken out of the bundle, with the claim checked on the instrument M-43 was built for rather than by a file listing: a boot fetches none of the four packs, by name and by path, and the drawer's first open fetches all four. The admission gate — every shipped pack priced through the same filesFor catalog-cost.mjs uses, and task one's arithmetic re-run rather than quoted, which is what found it understated. The materials — all 417 read for what can produce a colour, the four white models traced to their legacy ancestors at a25c9fd~1 and their named diffuse maps searched for across every commit in the repository, the colours sampled out of the photographs J1 retired and then verified by re-rendering to within three sRGB units. The selection — changed shape first and measured by the suite passing unaltered, before one new assertion was written. The winding — read off the three in node_modules rather than assumed. The stack reach — taken from J1's own six measured heights rather than chosen. What was not run: no pack was acquired, so every figure about what J2 will admit is still a projection from this tree's numbers. Three of this document set's own records are corrected in place: task one's claim that 1.5× reaches only the top of RM-007's range without curation — it reaches neither end — and two claims about mirror and about the winding that measurement moved rather than confirmed. Four repository faults were found by running things rather than reading them, and all four are fixed: duplicateSelected, which had never once worked; Main.showItemSelected's half duck-type guard, which admitted an object it would throw on one click later; halfSize going negative under a mirror, which would have cut a wall hole of negative width; and Item.showError, dead since the fork, now the collision warning. And one was found by a test fake: the stub that returned the shape its caller wished for is now pinned against the real method's key set, which is the durable half of that repair.

Method — RM-012, J3 delivery. The last sprint of the programme, and every figure below was produced by running something. X-7 re-measured rather than quoted — model/scene.js read for the loaders it constructs (four) and the sprint's own diff read for the loaders it wrote (none). The census — every .glb in public/models opened and its JSON chunk parsed: 202 of 215 declare Draco, and 72 of 215 name an images[].uri or buffers[].uri that is not a data URI, which is the measurement that put the external-reference warning in the import dialog and disproved the assumption that a .glb is self-contained. The save format — one item record serialized with and without the local key: 217 bytes and 291, so 74. The bounds — Scene.measureModel and a real placement run against the same file in headless Chromium and held to each other to five decimal places, which is K1's finding applied before it could recur. The store — the repository driven through write, list, read, remove and clear against the suite's fake IDBFactory and again against Chromium's own, with indexedDB.databases() read directly for the third-database claim, and a Draco-compressed import placed from bytes to prove the decoder is reached. The round trip — a model imported, placed, saved, and the document loaded into a second Model on the same store, with the size, the scale and the axis compared item to item. The payload — npm run build:demo and npm run budget:update in a detached worktree at b4f9ae8 and again here, because subtracting one figure from another is how K1's number went wrong; the predecessor re-measured at 421,549 bytes, matching what K3 recorded. The knock-on — npm run admit re-run, which is how the 15,216 bytes off the catalog's admission headroom were found rather than assumed to be zero. What was not run: no .fbx, no .usdz and no external-texture resolution — the import reads what a file points at and reports it, and does nothing to go and get it, because a browser cannot read the directory a file came from. Three faults were found in the suite's own IndexedDB fake and all three are fixed: a JSON clone that rendered an ArrayBuffer as {}, a quota weigher that therefore priced a 30 MB model at two bytes and made the refusal unreachable, and a transaction that did not roll back on abort. And one jsdom artefact is recorded rather than worked around in production code: vitest's jsdom environment has two ArrayBuffer constructors, so data instanceof ArrayBuffer inside GLTFLoader fails for a buffer Node produced — the copy that fixes it is in the fixture reader and in the fake, not in _parseModel, because defending shipped code against a test environment's realm split would cost a copy of every model on every load.

Method — RM-014. Seven measurements against the working tree at ab7e466 on branch amit, every one produced by running something. The words — an extractor over every .vue and .js file in src/: template text nodes with {{ }} removed and punctuation-only nodes dropped, the four attributes a person reads, and the literals handed to toasts.* and throw new Error; deduplicated, keyed, and gzipped at level 9 through the same call the budget tool makes. It undercounts sentences assembled from variables, which is stated with the number rather than after it, and the next measurement is how often that happens. The library's own English — src/scripts censused separately by the four routes it actually uses to reach a person: failed(…), a validation problem's message, console.error and a thrown Error. The assembly — every toasts.* call classified as a whole string or a template literal carrying a ${}. The units — Dimensioning.cmToMeasure read branch by branch for what it concatenates, and every toLocaleString site in the tree counted. The keyboard — every listener the floorplanner attaches enumerated from attachTo, keyDown and keyUp read for what they actually do, and tabindex counted across src/app. The motion — the prefers-reduced-motion block read against a count of every animation, @keyframes and transition declaration in both stylesheets, and the tree grepped for motion produced in JavaScript. The help surface — AppTip uses, binding entries, stable ids and Reka imports counted, and docs/ read page by page for who it addresses. The headroom — taken from tools/budget.json after J3's own budget:update, not from a previous drawing. What was not run: no translation of anything — there is no second language in this repository, so every figure about what L3 produces is a projection from the English census; no screen reader, so L4's claims are about focus, keys and axe rather than about what NVDA announces; and no tour, so L2's cost is an estimate of writing, which is the one thing in this document set that has never been measured well. One clause of RM-007 is recorded as already delivered rather than planned: L4's reduced motion, which one media query has covered since the shell was written — the sprint keeps only the exception CSS cannot reach.

Method — RM-018. Seven measurements against the working tree at 2909594 on branch amit, every one produced by running something. The gate — npm run test:coverage twenty-one consecutive times on one clean commit, in four batches, on an otherwise idle machine; the flake is a race, so a loaded machine measures a different one. Which file moves — six of those runs had their coverage-summary.json kept and compared file by file on all four metrics, which is what turned “the gate flakes” into “one file of 169 moves”. Which line — the statement and branch maps read out of coverage-final.json, so the line number comes from the instrument rather than from reading the file. Who builds the loaders — each of the twelve suites that mention addItem or measureModel run alone with coverage, twice or three times each, and then a recorder installed on createModelLoaders that writes the value of support and the current test file on every call, over four more full runs. The slack — all nineteen floors computed as covered − ceil(floor × total) against a clean run's own numbers, which is the calculation that makes a ten-branch directory legible. The budget — both builds remade from clean at 2909594 and again in a detached worktree at 65fa12b, because subtracting one recorded figure from another is how RM-013 K1's number went wrong. The rest of the board — seven check scripts, npm audit twice, npm outdated, and the browser tier run three times and timed. Two probes were written and thrown away, both instrumenting loaders.js; the first swallowed its own failures in a catch and therefore reported nothing in exactly the runs that were interesting, which is why the second one cannot throw. What was not run: no measurement on a second machine, so AD-3's premise — that a probe context and a renderer can disagree — is taken from three's own reasoning and from the comment at main.js:552, not from a case where they did; no bisect to the commit that first made the gate able to fail, because the two ingredients are known by construction — loaders.js did not exist before M3 and the statements floor was 87 until N2 set it to 89 — and a bisect over a one-in-three flake needs more runs per commit than the answer is worth; and nothing against a deployed page, for the seventh drawing running.

Method — RM-017, P2 delivery. The audit — axe-core over the whole document with the rule set and the two exclusions the six existing cases use, each panel reached by selecting the thing it inspects and each dialog by opening it; the screen count read off the tree with import.meta.glob rather than written down. The three defects — each one reported by the tool with its rule id and its nodes, fixed, and confirmed by a deliberate break that restores it. The five cases that were auditing nothing — found by printing every heading in the document during the corner case and getting back one h1; the panels render an h2, so their absence was the whole diagnosis. Five deliberate breaks across both sprints of this programme. Not run: no screen reader, so what is asserted is what a static audit can see and not what a person hears; no keyboard-order audit, because L4 delivered and gated that and P2 does not revisit it; and five screens are unaudited by name, because each needs an item placed in the scene.

Method — RM-017, P1 delivery. Choosing the boxes — a throwaway probe that rasters the same scene with the feedback present and deleted and prints the changed-pixel count for four candidate regions, which is where the 921/407 and 417/405 come from; the boxes in the committed file are the ones that measurement chose rather than ones that looked right. The fossils — src/scripts grepped for six phrasings of "this does not work", each hit read, and the one live line the survivors sit above counted in the coverage report: 205 executions for mergeWithIntersected. Three deliberate breaks — the label deleted, the arc deleted with the label kept, and the unit conversion bypassed; the first two each caught a pixel assertion that was measuring the rubber band, and the assertions were rewritten rather than the breaks abandoned. Not run: no assertion that the label is legible rather than merely present, which would need glyph recognition and is not what a raster can do; and nothing about where the label sits, because moving it is a product decision with no finding behind it.

Method — RM-017. Six measurements against the working tree at fad8333 on branch amit, every one produced by running something. The bindings — a throwaway probe that mounts the application, swaps each of the 46 bindings' run for a recorder, synthesises the browser event for its declared combination (accelerator from the module's own IS_APPLE, and the browser spellings for space, escape and the arrows) and dispatches it at window; the probe was written twice, because the first version reported 21 failures that were all correctly-disabled bindings and the second asks the question that matters — is any binding enabled and silent. The shared state — every owner.ref.value = in src/app attributed to its file, and the 49 watchers counted; the caveat that this cannot see AB-9 is measured rather than assumed, because AB-9's own file shows no such assignment. The drawing feedback — the block read, then the coverage report queried at its exact line numbers, twice: once over two suites, where it is never executed, and once over all 89, where it runs once. The axe gap — the six cases counted against the components that render a screen. Not run: no attempt to build a tool that follows method calls into composables, which is what a scan able to find AB-9 would need and which is not worth it at 49 watchers; nothing against a deployed page, for the sixth drawing running; and no measurement of whether this application is pleasant to use, which is still the largest unmeasured thing here and still needs somebody other than its author to open it.

Method — RM-016, N3 delivery. The index arithmetic — all four pack files re-encoded three ways in one pass, gzip level 9 each time, so the 156 bytes and the 48 bytes are differences between builds of the same content rather than estimates; the index/detail split measured in the same pass. The new limit — derived from Lighthouse's own mobile throttle, 1,638.4 Kbps, which is the figure the gate this project already runs uses; 50,000 bytes at that rate is 244 ms. The rule — exercised against fifteen URLs, eight that must fail and seven that must pass, including the repository's own github.com link, plus the README this repository actually ships. One deliberate break: the Live app button put back, which fails deploy:check and the headless case. Not run: no DNS lookup in the gate, deliberately — a network check in a build gate is a red mark on a train, and the finding it would catch is the one the shape rule catches offline; nothing against a deployed page, for the sixth drawing running; and no attempt to shrink the detail files, which are 59 % of the line and are licence text.

Method — RM-016, N2 delivery. The bug — a mounted application traced tick by tick, the camera mode and the workspace layout printed after the call, after one tick and after settling; the fix then verified by the case that found it rather than by re-reading the code. Where the coverage was — the branch map of the three files read out of coverage-final.json line by line, which is what showed the uncovered half to be almost entirely failure arms rather than logic. The directory floors — the coverage report aggregated per directory, each floor taken as the largest multiple of five strictly below the measurement. That M-57 is load-bearing — two runs with the new App suite deleted: with the real global floors it fails four checks and proves nothing, and with the globals relaxed to where a few sprints of growth would leave them it fails exactly one, the directory floor at 38.15 % against 60. Not run: no mutation testing, so “every new case fails against a deliberate break” is asserted for the suites that were deleted wholesale and not case by case; nothing against a deployed page, for the fifth drawing running; and no attempt at the remaining 35 % of App.vue, which is the share and draft-recovery paths and would need repository fakes this sprint did not price.

Method — RM-016, N1 delivery. Both floors — five runs of the gate against one build, desktop 96, 96, 96, 95 and mobile 62, 62, 63, 62, 62, which is what turned the floor rule from “rounded down to the nearest 5” into a stated two-point margin; the desktop figure comes from Lighthouse's own desktop-config, imported rather than transcribed. M-56's table — all seven shipped designs mounted in a real viewer in headless Chromium, three seconds for the furniture to arrive over the network, then renderer.info.render read and 30 frames timed; the wait is three seconds because an earlier pass waited 300 ms and recorded 61 calls for a design that costs 187. Two deliberate breaks: stopping the base batch failed the five unfurnished rows, and stopping the model loader failed exactly the two furnished ones and nothing else. Not run: nothing on a deployed page, for the fourth drawing running; no re-measurement of the 400-wall fixture, which was left exactly as M2 set it and is asserted to have been by its own unchanged test.

Method — RM-016. Six measurements against the working tree at c2f6eec on branch amit, every one produced by running something rather than by reading code. Lighthouse twice — one build, one machine, one local server, the desktop and mobile presets back to back in a single process, so the 91 and the 62 differ only in the emulation. The desktop half used a throttling table written for this probe; N1's gate imports Lighthouse's own preset and reads 96. The probe was right about the gap and one point out of five about its size. The renderer on real designs — a Chromium probe that fetches each shipped .blueprint3d over HTTP, mounts a real Main, waits 2.5 seconds for the furniture to arrive over the network, then reads renderer.info and times 30 frames; the two-bedroom's 187 calls include its 19 items, and the probe was re-run after a first pass that waited only 300 ms and therefore counted 61. Coverage by area — the same coverage-summary.json CI gates on, aggregated per directory and per file. The catalog arithmetic — all 215 .glb files measured and averaged, both budget lines' headroom divided by the per-item cost. The address — a DNS lookup, with a control request to github.com from the same shell returning 200. RM-007's five — each re-run against the tree rather than assumed closed. Not run: nothing against a deployed page, for the third drawing running; no measurement of a person actually using this, which is the gap M-51 exists to close and the reason this drawing has no finding about usability at all; and no profiling of the 2D pass, which M2 measured six days ago and which nothing since has touched.

Method — RM-015, M3 delivery. Nine builds of this tree and three Lighthouse runs on each side of the change, all of them produced by running something. Where the payload goes — a probe build carrying a Rollup generateBundle hook that dumps every module's rendered length per chunk, at HEAD and after each boundary; the baseline it produced reproduces tools/budget.json's recorded 432,781 exactly, which is what makes the four figures in the table above comparable. What each loader costs — four builds, each with one loader stubbed out and the other three in place, so no figure is a subtraction from another. Lighthouse — the assembled tree served over HTTP from localhost, Playwright's chromium, three runs of the current build (62, 62, 61) and two of a pristine git worktree at 09945f0 (56, 57); the before/after is two builds of the same tree on one machine within the same hour, not a figure read from a report. The eager graph — the browser tier's resource timings printed at import time, which is what produced AA-8. Five deliberate breaks, each run against the suite that should catch it, one of which was not caught and produced a test that does. Not run: nothing against a deployed page, because there still is not one — M-53's field half is written into deploy.yml and has never executed; no measurement on a real mobile device, since Lighthouse's throttling is a simulation and is named as one; and no second opinion on the score, which is one tool's weighting and is valuable here precisely because it is not ours.

Method — RM-015, M2 delivery, second half. Where the frame goes — every drawing phase of the 2D pass wrapped and accumulated over 20 draws after five warm-up blocks, at 400 walls and 150 items, then reported as a share of the whole. That table is the finding: drawGrid at 0.005 ms is what RM-007 proposed caching. How much is off screen — every wall projected through the view's own convertX/convertY and tested against the canvas rectangle: 245 of 400, with the plan 1,476 pixels wide in a 1,024 pixel viewport. The result — the same fixture timed in six blocks after culling, 1.285 / 1.20 / 1.17 / 1.155 / 1.10 / 1.12, and the gate's fixture then raised to 100 rooms permanently and run four times for stability. The false lead — the text-state cache, measured before and after at 1.98 and 1.95 ms and kept anyway, recorded as not being the reason the gate passes. Instancing — measured rather than assumed before deferring: 972 bare, 1,272 with 150 items, 2 per item exactly, and 974 if all 150 collapsed to one call, which is still above 802. The breaks — four against the culling suite, all caught. What was not run: no attempt at M-52's remaining calls, and no instancing; both wait on the same change to how a face fades. And one thing checked rather than assumed: that culling cannot reach an export — renderTo sets exporting and is the single door the SVG export, the PNG export and K1's thumbnails all use.

Method — RM-015, M2 delivery. The batch — measured in headless Chromium off renderer.info.render at 144 and 400 walls, before and after, with the scene traversed and meshes counted by name; the triangle count is reported beside the call count precisely because it does not move, which is what says the picture is unchanged. What could be batched — decided by reading updateVisibility rather than by trying: it writes material.opacity per edge over planes, so the two populations that can share a mesh are the ones that never enter that loop and the ones that always leave it together. The 2D conditional — AA-4's rule run as written. Walls alone at 400 measured five times, 1.995 / 1.73 / 1.615 / 1.51 / 1.51, warm 1.51; the gate's own fixture with its 150 footprints then measured 2.165 against 2. Both numbers are kept because the first one alone would have declined the cache and the second is why it is needed. The budget breach — attributed by building the library twice, at M1 and with the change, rather than by assuming the delta was the sprint's: it was 807 of 4,120. What was not run: the cached static layer, which AA-4's conditional now requires and which is recorded as outstanding rather than described as declined; and no attempt at M-52's remaining 170 draw calls, which need per-edge fading to stop being a property of a material. One deliberate non-change: the r98 goldens, which pin edge.planes at five entries and which shaped the implementation instead of being edited by it.

Method — RM-015, M1 delivery. What the sprint ran that the drawing could not. The policy at two bases — strategyFor called for six paths under https://amitukind.github.io/architect3d/ and under https://architect3d.pages.dev/ and the answers printed side by side; they agree on all six, which is what turned AA-2's “the worker hard-codes nothing” from a reading of the source into a measurement, and the root half is now a suite beside the sub-path one. The gate — run against a genuinely assembled tree, built and moved exactly as the workflow does it, then five deliberate breaks: assets rewritten under a sub-path, sw.js renamed to a hashed filename, start_url made root-absolute, a live link to the retired host appended to the README, and a README link to a file that does not exist. All five failed the gate; the first is the base-path mistake the gate exists for. The correction — the first real run failed on the roadmap itself, and the rule was narrowed from mentions to links rather than the roadmap being edited to satisfy it. What was not run: the deploy. There is no Cloudflare account or token in this environment and no network publish was attempted, so M-51 is outstanding and every claim about what the deployed site does is a projection — which is the same limit RM-015 recorded before the sprint started, unchanged by having built it. The artifact is checked; the address is not yet asserted.

Method — RM-015. Seven measurements against the working tree at 7012618 on branch amit, every one produced by running something. The address — two HTTP requests to the URLs the README advertises, with the status codes taken off the responses; the nine links counted in README.md; deploy.yml read for its trigger and its own account of why. The base surface — the whole tree grepped for the repository sub-path and each hit classified as production or test, then sw.js, useOffline.js and cache_policy.js read for how the scope is obtained. The renderer — a probe in headless Chromium building real plans through Model.loadSerialized at one and thirty-six rooms, with and without 150 items added through Scene.addItem and a stub loader, reading renderer.info.render.calls, .triangles and info.memory.geometries, timing thirty frames after a warm render, and traversing the scene to census meshes by name. The 2D pass — view.draw() timed over twenty runs after one warm draw, at 144, 196 and 400 walls. The payload — every emitted chunk gzipped at level 9 and the document parsed for what it references, then a second build of this tree with a manualChunks rule added and nothing else changed. The split that failed — every module id reaching the hook logged, filtered and counted; a first pass truncated that list at eight lines and drew the opposite conclusion, which is recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because the wrong version was one head away from being written down as a finding. Lighthouse — package.json, .github/ and tools/ grepped. What was not run: no Cloudflare deploy, so every figure about M1's outcome is a projection and M-51 is the first thing that will test it; no Lighthouse, because there is no deployed page to point one at, which is why M3's floor is recorded on first measurement rather than chosen here; and no reading of the Actions history — gh is not authenticated in this environment, so the claim that Deploy has never published is taken from deploy.yml's own header, written by RM-006, rather than from the run log. The 404s are measured; the never is cited.

Method — RM-014, L4 delivery. What the sprint ran that the drawing could not. The event surface — mousedown, mousemove and mouseup read for every field they touch on the object they are handed, which is what decided that a synthetic press is two numbers rather than a PointerEvent: clientX, clientY, and pointerType for the touch branch. The projection — asserted rather than reasoned about, to nine decimal places, with the pane placed at (137, 89) so that a version dropping the bounds offset could not round-trip past it. The 3D key binding — measured on a live OrbitControls by wrapping _handleKeyDown and counting calls for each of three targets under each of two bindings, which is the table in L4's landing block and the reason a characterization test was re-pointed rather than relaxed. The four deliberate breaks — the bounds offset, the move inside moveCursor, the move inside placeCursor and the release inside hideCursor, each deleted in turn against the finished suite. The third one exposed a hole rather than confirming a gate: it broke nothing, because the call it removed was genuinely dead and the test written for it placed a corner, which mousedown positions by itself. The dead call is gone, and the test now deletes a wall — the one thing that needs the hover state only a move can set. M-50 — a capture-phase tripwire on window over fifteen event types, read after a keyboard-only session in Chromium. What was not run: no screen reader, so every claim here is about focus, keys and axe rather than about what NVDA announces — the same limit RM-014 recorded before the programme started, unchanged by having built it. And one repository finding is recorded rather than fixed, for the second sprint running: the browser tier registers no Tailwind plugin and runs unstyled, which is why L4's focus-ring assertion is about :focus-visible and not about a computed outline.

Method — RM-014, L3 withdrawal. The sprint was cancelled mid-flight on 2026-08-20, after its scaffold had been committed as f283d5c and before its language files existed. The revert — git revert over the whole commit rather than a hand-picked unwind, then git write-tree compared against git rev-parse cf70abb^{tree}: both e711695, which is the only form of “fully reverted” worth claiming. The tree after it — lint, typecheck and ledger:check run clean, the ledger back at its pre-L3 162, and vitest run at 2,601 passed in 82 files. The leftovers — src/, tests/ and tools/ grepped for i18n, useI18n, core/messages, runtime.text and decimalSeparator: no match anywhere. The reach — git branch --contains f283d5c, which names amit and origin/amit only, so nothing deployed ever carried it. What was not run: no fresh build and no budget:update — deliberately, because a tree identical to a measured tree cannot have a different payload, and re-measuring it would produce a number that looks like evidence and is really a tautology. What is kept rather than deleted: the whole L3 card, its acceptance gate, and findings Z-1 to Z-4 — struck, annotated, and left where a later reader will find them, because the measurements are facts about this tree and only the plan was withdrawn.

Method — RM-014, L2 delivery. What the sprint ran that the drawing could not, since every figure about L2's own output was a projection until it existed. The anchors — checked three ways rather than once, because each catches what the others cannot: every id= in src/app grepped by npm run help:check, every step asserted for a title, a body and a layout that exists, and every anchor resolved against a mounted shell in Chromium, which is the only one of the three that can tell a rendered id from a written one. The evidence check — run on a cold Chromium profile with all three databases deleted first, which is what failed and what produced the finding: indexedDB.databases() lists all three after boot because the application creates them, so existence was measuring that the application had started. The empty states — the catalog driven into each of its four empty conditions and the rendered sentence read, including the recent list whose kit has not loaded, which is the one that cannot be reached by clicking an empty chip. The payload — npm run build:demo then npm run budget:update, and the delta taken against J3's own recorded figure rather than estimated: +2,996 gzipped bytes. The words — counted by the gate that checks them, 2,225 over four pages, and none of them in the payload. What was not run: no screen reader and no usability test — axe passes on all six tour steps in all three layouts, and nothing in that says the tour teaches anybody anything, which is the one claim this sprint makes that a repository cannot check. One of this document set's own numbers is corrected in place: Z-1's remaining headroom, which L2 has since spent 2,996 bytes of. And one repository finding is recorded rather than fixed: the browser tier registers no Tailwind plugin and therefore runs unstyled, which makes getBoundingClientRect useless as a visibility test there — nothing existing depends on it, and L2's own check reads an inline pane width instead.

Method — RM-011, delivery. What H1 ran that the drawing above could not, since every figure about H1's own output was a projection until it existed. Task one and the material model are recorded in the LANDING block. The library — thirty CC0 materials fetched from the Poly Haven API at 1K, each map decoded, resampled in linear light through resize-textures.mjs's own resampler and re-encoded, then gated by that pass's own two gates: lowFrequency against the 1K source, which catches a gamma slip or a channel swap, and pixelRms against the pixels that went into the encoder, which is codec generation loss and nothing else. 60 shipped images, 60 measurements, and the counts asserted equal. The resolution — six materials round-tripped through 1024, 512, 256 and 128 and the surviving detail reported in dB, which is what separated the albedo from the roughness map rather than a preference. The quality — not measured again: resize-textures.mjs measured this tree's JPEG knee at 95 and the argument transfers unchanged, so the number does. The scene's cost — sceneVram() computed from the catalogs, the fixtures and the .glb image tables in Node, then held to renderer.info.memory in Chromium on a scene with a real library material on its walls and its floor. What was not run: no KTX2 encode of the library — the trial had already measured the codec and the reason for JPEG is the transcoder's 515 KB rather than the codec's fidelity; no normal map, for the reason W-12 measured; and no pixel comparison against a golden, because the library is new content and there is nothing frozen to compare it to. One earlier record was corrected: W-12's 8.8 MB and 1.5×, above, which priced one map under a two-map heading. Two repository inaccuracies were found and fixed rather than recorded, since this is a delivery pass: kindOf in the manifest generator called every unmatched file a texture, which the VRAM budget then asked for dimensions; and the served manifest carried 17,065 gzipped bytes of integrity hashes for a feature nothing turns on. The first load — the built document parsed for the scripts and stylesheets it references, each gzipped at level 9 with asset-manifest.json beside them, which is W-7's method with the file list read from the document rather than from a directory; and a boot's performance.getEntriesByType('resource') filtered for the library, in Chromium, with the whole catalog's urls checked rather than a sample.

Method — RM-010, delivery. What the three sprints ran that the drawing above could not, since every figure about their own output was an estimate until they existed. G1 and G2 are recorded in their LANDED blocks. G3 — a three-storey fixture generated through the real Model by tools/make-fixtures.mjs and then driven: loaded, re-saved and compared as strings, twice and into a document that already held a design; committed to and undone through useHistory; written and read back through useAutosave; drawn on the plan and exported as SVG once per storey; and loaded into headless Chromium, where the frame was read off the drawing buffer with readPixels before and after hiding the upper storeys, and all eight corners of buildingBounds() were tested against the camera's frustum. V-7 — exportSerialized().length at one, two and three storeys, and the same call timed over 200 iterations after 20 warm ones; useHistory.stats() after ten commits. V-8 — per-file coverage-summary.json, before and after, for the six files the finding names. V-10 — the fixture script re-run and git diff read, then a seeded Floorplan constructed with a counting random source to find where the eight draws go. What was not run: no pixel comparison against a golden — the browser tier asserts that the frame changed and by how much, not that it is a particular picture; and the autosave figure is the serialisation only, because the write itself is IndexedDB's and asynchronous since RM-003 A5. The two inaccuracies above were half cleared and half corrected: the comment is gone, and buildRoofUniformHeight() stays because it carries a frozen r98 golden — recorded in G2's block. One earlier record was corrected: RM-008 E1's claim about setSelectedObject(null), in G3's block.

Sources — RM-009. Kenney — Furniture Kit (CC0) · three.js — Shape · three.js — ShapeGeometry · glTF 2.0 specification

Sources — RM-008. MDN — CanvasRenderingContext2D · W3C — SVG 2 · MDN — requestAnimationFrame

Sources — RM-007. Coohom — Floor Planner · Sweet Home 3D — Features · Kenney — Furniture Kit (CC0) · Poly Haven (CC0) · ambientCG (CC0) · Quaternius (CC0) · three.js documentation · MDN — Service Worker API · MDN — IndexedDB

Method — RM-013. Eight measurements against the working tree at 2879133 on branch amit, all of them produced by running something. The store — IndexedDbDraftRepository pointed at the suite's own fake IDBFactory pre-set to version 2, then put, read and stats called and their returns printed; and the opposite direction opened at version 2 against a factory at version 1 with the upgrade event observed. The identity — DEFAULT_DESIGN parsed for its top-level keys, then the same document with name, id, createdAt and modifiedAt added put through the real DesignDocument.parse and the constructed document's own fields enumerated. The sheet — a Floorplanner2D built on a 400 × 300 room and a second on an 1180 × 860 flat, then exportPlanSVG called in all three pairings under jsdom and the <path> elements counted in each. The thumbnail — renderPlanToCanvas run in headless Chromium at 200, 300 and 480 px and each canvas handed to toBlob as PNG, WebP q85 and JPEG q82, with the byte counts taken off the blobs rather than estimated. The starter plans — five distinct floorplans built with newCorner and newWall, closed, updated, serialized through saveFloorplan with fourteen item records each, and gzipped at level 9. The quota — navigator.storage.estimate() and indexedDB.databases() read in Chromium on a cold profile. The link — the same designs at four furniture counts through gzip -9 and brotli q11, then base64url encoded and the characters counted. The footprint — src/app grepped for the boot path and for every download filename. What was not run: no service worker and no .zip, so nothing above prices K3 or K2's bundle beyond the fragment arithmetic.

Method — RM-013, K1 delivery. What the sprint ran that the drawing above could not, since every figure about K1's own output was a projection until it existed. The export repair — the two functions given a view and a floorplan that disagree, then the whole headless suite re-run and its three failures traced to their setups rather than to the change; each failing test re-read for what it had actually been asserting. The store — the repository driven through write, list, read, rename, duplicate and delete against the suite's fake IDBFactory and again against Chromium's own, with indexedDB.databases() read directly for the two-database claim and eight 40-item designs written to measure what a listing costs against what it stores. The templates — five plans built by calling Floorplan.newCorner and newWall, closed, updated and serialized, then every one of the seven documents put through DesignDocument.parse and its error and warning counts printed; the gzipped total taken by the budget tool it was added to. The furniture — each sample loaded in headless Chromium and every item's position.y, halfSize.y and objectHalfSize().y printed beside what the document asked for, which is how the accessor union was found to disagree with three.js on four of fifteen rows and how the scene-graph walk that replaced it was confirmed to agree on all fifteen. The tile — renderPlanThumbnail drawn into a recording canvas and its calls searched for the north arrow's own label. Coverage — npm run test:coverage, all four figures read and one floor raised. What was not run: nothing about K2 or K3, and no visual comparison of a thumbnail — the tile is asserted by its size, its aspect and what it does not draw, not by its pixels.

Method — RM-013, K2 delivery. Eight measurements before a line was written and four more on the way out, all run. The link — every document this build ships compressed with gzip -9 and brotli q11 and base64url'd, then the same designs put through Chromium's own CompressionStream in both gzip and deflate-raw and the outputs compared byte for byte against Node's. The ceiling — history.replaceState driven at six lengths from 2,000 to 2,000,000 characters in Chromium and location.hash read back after each. The read-only surface — the plan's six modes read for what each mutates, src/app grepped for the 35 keyboard bindings and the 20 inspector files, and Controller.enabled traced to its one existing owner. The bundle — the asset closure of the largest sample walked from the document and each file's size taken off disk. The payload — npm run build:demo and tools/check-budget.mjs run in a detached worktree at four separate commits, because the alternative was subtracting one figure from another and that is exactly how K1's number went wrong. What was not run: no third-party zip tool opened a bundle written here — the container is asserted against the format's own signatures and round-tripped through Chromium's deflate, which is what a recipient's build would use, but nothing in this pass proves Finder agrees.

Method — RM-013, K3 delivery. Six measurements before a line was written, and one command that is the sprint. The boot — the application mounted in headless Chromium and performance.getEntriesByType('resource') read: 7 runtime resources, 814,585 bytes, of which the Basis transcoder is 585 KB, pulled in because the boot design's ground is a .ktx2. The deploy — every file in dist-demo/ walked and bucketed: 601 files, 20,547,813 B, of which 8 source maps are 7,408,803 B — 36.1 %; the shell is 10 files and 1,522,931 B, so a complete offline copy is 2,337,516 B, 11.4 % of the deploy. The platform — serviceWorker, caches and onbeforeinstallprompt probed in the browser rather than assumed, and the existing registrations counted (zero). The icons — rendered, then decoded with pngjs and their pixels counted: 192×192 and 512×512, ink on 6.5 % and 6.9 % of the tile, corners the accent colour so a maskable crop keeps the glyph. The worker — npm run offline:check: dist-demo/ served from a Node server with no-store on everything, the browser taken offline with context.setOffline(true) rather than the server stopped, the page reloaded and interrogated, and a redeploy simulated with a server overlay. What was not run: no Lighthouse and no installability audit — the manifest is checked field by field and the icons are checked pixel by pixel, but nothing here proves Chrome would offer the install on a given day, because that is a heuristic and not a contract.

Method — RM-011. Eleven measurements against the working tree at 385aa88 on branch amit, five of them run in headless Chromium against the library as the dev server serves it, and none of them quoted from a specification. The materials — the three-storey fixture loaded into a viewer and every mesh in the scene traversed for its material's class and for which of eight map slots is set, run once per render profile, which is how “the walls are unlit” became a table rather than a reading of a docblock. The surface record — Wall, Room and Floorplan read for what a texture is, the fixture round-tripped, and the pickable surfaces counted per storey. The budgets — limits and last measurements taken from tools/budget.json, headroom subtracted, and every projection computed as image count times the measured mean of this tree's own encoded files: 36,182 B over the ten .ktx2 and 110,732 B over the nine the oracle refused, with VRAM through check-budget.mjs's own texels × 4/3 formula. The scene's real cost — renderer.info.memory read in Chromium after a settled render, for the unfurnished house and for a twenty-item design. The frame — twenty frames timed after five warm ones at 1024 × 768 under SwiftShader, both profiles, both designs. The first load — the demo build's four entry files gzipped at level 9, then a boot's performance.getEntriesByType('resource') read to find what is fetched after them. The shadow filter — renderer.shadowMap.type read back after boot and compared with what main.js assigns. The rest — catalog keys counted over all 168 entries, which ktx toktx basisu, and the tree grepped for a cube camera. What was not run: no encoder, again, and this time it is the finding rather than the caveat — ktx, toktx and basisu are all absent from this machine, exactly as they were when RM-004 B1 said so, which is why W-6 reasons from the refusal ledger RM-006 measured rather than from a new encode, and why H1's first task is the trial. No material was authored and no light was moved, so every figure about H1's and H2's own output is a projection from this tree's numbers. Two repository inaccuracies were found and are recorded rather than fixed, since this is a planning pass: three/main.js:301 assigns a shadow filter three no longer implements and silently downgrades (W-8), and RM-007 assigns wall collision to both H3 and J4 (W-11). Both are H2's and H3's to clear. Two of this document set's own metrics are corrected here: M-28, which passes at 12.9× its target, and the instrument behind texture-vram, which measures a tree the programme is about to stop resembling.
